drivers.variant_notes: The only physical Class of 1812 driver (gprom.bin with the yrom1, drom1, arom1 and arom2 sound ROMs), declared INITGAME(clas1812, ALPHA, FLIP67, 3/*?*/, SNDBRD_GTS3, 4) in pinned src/wpc/gts3games.c lines 217-226 and catalogued with CORE_GAMEDEFNV(clas1812, "Class of 1812", 1991, "Gottlieb", mGTS3S, 0). Its power-up screen reads CLASS OF 1812 / 730 88FB, and 730 is IPDB's model number for the machine. Every runtime probe here ran on it, and the known-working script loads it (cGameName = "clas1812"). Its only clone, beav_butt, is a VPX-only reskin that scope.py excludes.

physical.notes: GTS3_SWDIAG on the cabinet port (internal column 0). On alpha generation 1, which MACHINE_INIT(gts3) sets for this driver, SWITCH_UPDATE drives VIA U4 CA1 with it. Every retained self-test run steps through the tests with it: the first press at 1 shows the self-test 1 prompt (bookkeeping and game adjustments) and each further press steps to the next self-test, up to 9, the Front Door Test (runs nvram-init, lamp-matrix, solenoids, switch-matrix, front-door). Class1812.vbs names it swDiagnostic = -8.

GTS3_SWTILT on the cabinet port, read through alpha_u4_pb_r on VIA U4 PB4 without inversion. Held at 1 inside the Switch Matrix Test it replaced the switch line with TILT (run switch-matrix), so the ROM reads it active at 1. Class1812.vbs names it swTilt = -7. The known-working script sets vpmNudge.TiltSwitch = 151 (line 112), which is not this address or any address System 3 publishes, so its nudge tilt pulses nothing the ROM reads: a defect in that table.

GTS3_SWSLAM on the cabinet port, read on alpha generation 1 through alpha_u4_pb_r on VIA U4 PB3 without inversion. A pulse at 1 inside the Front Door Test ended the test and left the displays showing the score screen (run front-door), so the ROM reads it active at 1. Class1812.vbs names it swSlamTilt = -6.

physical.location: CPU board auxiliary connector (optional communications adapter)
physical.notes: GTS3_SWPRIN, which PinMAME reads back into the printer status that aux1_r returns for the optional communications adapter (printer) on the CPU board's auxiliary connector: at 1 the status reads ready, at 0 not connected. It is not a matrix switch, and held at 1 inside the Switch Matrix Test it put no line of its own on the display, which still showed the previous step's RIGHT FLIPPER =07 (run switch-matrix). A recreation without the adapter leaves it at 0.

Strobe 0, return 0. In the Switch Matrix Test, holding public 0 at 1 alone displayed the ROM's name "LEFT COIN CHUTE" with =00 (run switch-matrix). In play, the Front Door Test counted a coin on the left chute (L) for each of two pulses at 1 (run front-door). Class of 1812's game data sets no inverted-switch mask and gts3.c's xvia_0_a_r hands the CPU the complement of the matrix column, so public 1 is the closed contact the CPU sees, and the Switch Matrix Test reads ALL SWITCHES OPEN with every address at 0: the matrix contact rests open and closes when the device is actuated. Class1812.vbs names it swCoin1 = 00 and its help text the left coin chute; GTS3_COMPORTS rewrites it from a coin key only with PinMAME keyboard handling on. The Front Door Test counts all three chutes, but doors differ: IPDB photo 5 shows a door with two coin slots and photo 24 a French door with one, and no source says which of the three inputs a given door wires, so how many chutes a machine has depends on its door.

physical.location: matrix copy of the cabinet flipper button
physical.notes: Strobe 0, return 6. In the Switch Matrix Test, holding the flipper button 143 at 1 displayed the ROM's name "LEFT FLIPPER" with =06 (run switch-matrix). physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (internal column 15, which core_updateSw uses for GEN_GTS3), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 140 through gts3_m2sw(15, row) = 140 + row. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS, and FLIP_SWNO(6,7) does not, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A drained ball lands on the OUTHOLE switch (54); the OUTHOLE coil (29) kicks it into the trough, and BALL RELEASE (28) feeds the lead ball into the shooter lane, where SHOOTER LANE (43) sees it waiting at the plunger. The ROM reads TROUGH (44) at 1 as both balls home. With 44 held at 1 throughout, a tilt ended the ball at once and the ROM released the next ball with the tilted one still out; with 44 opened after the release, the ROM waited after the tilt, kicked the outhole when 54 rose and served the next ball only once 44 had closed again (runs tilt-trough-closed and tilt-trough-open). That places 44 at the trough's second position, behind the ball waiting at the release, covered only while both balls are home. At Start the ROM reset both banks, energized the Q relay (32) and energized 28 for about 0.5 s. When 54 rose it released 32 and the display read YOU DUG UP 1 STIFF; once the host had opened 54 and closed 44 again it fired 29, reset both banks, energized 32 and 28 and began ball 2 (run gameplay). The script models the trough as two kickers, Slot1 at the release and Slot2 behind it, and the outhole as the Drain kicker (writing 54). It writes 44 from Slot1, a table defect that lets a tilt put a second ball in play; its 3.0.21 update writes 44 from Slot2. The known-working script models no ball lock: it holds balls only in the trough, the outhole and the two kickers (lines 112-147 and 226-274), and plays wire-ramp sounds for both ramps' exits (lines 769-788).
mechanisms.label: Outhole, two-ball trough, ball release and shooter lane

mechanisms.behavior: Four drop targets, L DROP TARGET 1-4 (16, 26, 36, 46), reset together by LEFT DROP T BANK (8). The ROM fired the reset at Start, when the fourth target went down and when it served ball 2, and completing the bank began a COUNTDOWN on the display; with L DT LIGHT LOCK (65) lit, it also turned 65 off, and R BB LOCK (47) flashed twice at once and again from about 12 s later (run gameplay). The instruction cards light the right ramp lock by completing the left drop targets when lit. The script's dtBankL writes the switches and raises the bank on 8.
mechanisms.label: Left four-target drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: Four drop targets, R DROP TARGET 1-4 (17, 27, 37, 47), reset together by RIGHT DROP T BANK (9). The ROM fired the reset at Start and when it served ball 2, and with all four held down it fired 9 seven times in about 2.7 s, retrying while the targets stayed down (run gameplay). The script's dtBankR writes the switches and raises the bank on 9.
mechanisms.label: Right four-target drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: Two ball holds: the BOTTOM UPKICKER (switch 52, coil 6), a scoop in the middle of the playfield, and the TOP KICKER (switch 53, coil 7) at the upper left, with the TOP KICKER RO rollover (55) on the lane above it. Held at 1 for 8 s during a game, 52 drew six pulses of 6 and 53 eight pulses of 7 (run gameplay): the ROM kicks again while its switch stays closed. The script models both as saucers and moves the scoop's sw52p primitive with 6. GATE (10) is a diverter flap the script turns about Primitive DiverterP above the top kicker. Unresolved: the instruction cards light the right ramp for a lock (complete the left drop targets when lit) and award an instant multiball from the door prize. In the scripted game, completing the left bank while L DT LIGHT LOCK (65) was lit turned 65 off; R BB LOCK (47) flashed twice at once, stayed dark until about 12 s later and then flashed through one pulse of the right ramp switch (50), which fired no gate and left 47 flashing. The host never closed the top kicker (53) afterwards. 10 rose only in the coil test, and the known-working script models no lock device. The ROM's full lock sequence, which path the gate opens, whether the top kicker holds the locked ball, and how the lock releases for multiball are therefore not known. A gameplay run that lights the lock and then writes the right ramp (50) and the top kicker (53) would show the ROM's sequence on 10, 7 and the ball release 28, but there the host supplies the ball path; the gate's physical route and where the ball is held need the manual, a factory drawing or an observation of a real machine.
mechanisms.label: Bottom upkicker, top kicker and gate

mechanisms.behavior: The two toys IPDB lists stand against the back panel at the rear of the playfield (IPDB photos 12 and 13), the chattering teeth on a bracket left of the beating heart. HEART (11) beats the heart and HEART 67 (2) (25) lights it from two bulbs; TEETH (12) works the jaw and lamp 2 (TEETH) lights the teeth. The ROM chattered the teeth in two bursts of pulses, sixteen from about 2.5 s to 8.2 s after Start, the first held about 1.1 s and the others 0.06-0.34 s, and thirteen of 0.06-0.07 s each over about 1.7 s, beginning within 0.1 s of the first of two spinner pulses 0.8 s apart (run gameplay). The script pumps the heart primitive once each time 11 turns on and holds the lower jaw at one angle while 12 is on and another while it is off.
mechanisms.label: Beating heart and chattering teeth

mechanisms.behavior: Three pop bumpers (switches 10, 11 and 12, coils 1, 2 and 3) and two kicking rubbers, the slingshots (switches 13 and 14, coils 4 and 5). System 3 has no special-solenoid circuit: the CPU reads each switch and fires its coil (40 ms pulses of each switch during a game fired its coil, run gameplay), so a consumer drives only the switch. The script assigns no callbacks to these coils and kicks with its own physics.
mechanisms.label: Pop bumpers and kicking rubbers

mechanisms.behavior: Two flippers. The cabinet buttons fire them through the flipper circuit while the Q relay (32) is energized, so no CPU driver appears for them in the solenoid test; PinMAME fabricates 45-48 from the buttons at 141 and 143 while 32 is on. The ROM reads the buttons as matrix switches 6 (LEFT FLIPPER) and 7 (RIGHT FLIPPER), which core_updateSw copies from 143 and 141.
mechanisms.label: Two flippers, cabinet-wired

mechanisms.behavior: The 'A' relay (26) switches the backbox lightbox illumination and the 'T' relay (31) the playfield G.I., which goes out while it is energized; PinMAME's System 3 init types them so, and the later 3.0.21 script drives the backglass and playfield G.I. from them. In the scripted game the ROM raised both with the flashers as the left bank and five spot targets scored (run gameplay). The KNOCKER (30) would be in the cabinet, but no retained source shows it fitted, and COIN MET/TIX COIL (27) drives an optional coin meter or ticket dispenser.
mechanisms.label: Relays, knocker and coin meter

physical.location: relay in the cabinet or backbox; it enables the flipper circuit
physical.notes: The Relay+Solenoid Test names driver 31 "Q" RELAY, and the credit button fired public 32 there (run solenoids; the displayed driver number is the public address minus one).
